parts.name: Crankshaft
parts.description: Turns the up-and-down push of the piston into rotation. Two heavy webs carry the crank pin 24.75 mm off-centre and act as counterweights. Everything else on this stand is driven from it: cam chain, starter clutch and flywheel on the left, balancer and primary gear on the right.

specs.label: Drives
specs.value: Cam chain, balancer, primary gear, flywheel

parts.name: Piston, rings and pin
parts.description: An aluminium piston sealed to the cylinder by two compression rings and an oil ring. The gudgeon pin joins it to the small end of the connecting rod. Combustion pressure on the crown is what drives the whole engine.

parts.name: Connecting rod
parts.description: Links the piston pin to the crank pin. Its small end only rocks back and forth while its big end follows the crank pin in a full circle on a caged needle bearing.

parts.name: Cylinder and head (outline)
parts.description: The finned cylinder barrel and cylinder head, drawn as a transparent outline so the piston and valves stay visible. The fins shed heat into the air stream. Toggle it under Show.

parts.name: Camshaft and cam sprocket
parts.description: Turns at exactly half crank speed, because each valve opens once every two crank revolutions. The 32-tooth sprocket is driven by the 16-tooth sprocket on the crank. Two lobes, one per valve, push the rocker arms.

parts.name: Exhaust rocker arm
parts.description: A lever on a fixed shaft. The cam lobe lifts one end and the other end presses the valve stem down, opening the valve. A screw adjuster sets the tappet clearance, the gap that has to be checked on every service.

parts.name: Exhaust valve and springs
parts.description: Lets the burnt gas out towards the exhaust pipe. It runs much hotter than the intake valve and is smaller because the gas leaves under pressure. Two nested springs snap it shut.

parts.name: Intake rocker arm
parts.description: A lever on a fixed shaft. The cam lobe lifts one end and the other end presses the valve stem down, opening the valve. A screw adjuster sets the tappet clearance, the gap that has to be checked on every service.

parts.name: Intake valve and springs
parts.description: Lets the fresh air and fuel mixture into the cylinder. It is the larger of the two valves because the mixture enters at low pressure. Two nested springs close it again as the cam lobe passes.

parts.name: Spark plug
parts.description: Needs more than 20,000 volts to jump its electrode gap. It fires a few degrees before top dead centre on the compression stroke, so the burning mixture reaches peak pressure just after the piston turns down.

parts.name: Cam chain, guide and tensioner
parts.description: A roller chain that keeps the camshaft locked to the crank at a 2 : 1 ratio, so the valves always open at the right moment. The crank pulls the front run tight against a fixed guide; a sprung slipper on the slack rear run takes up stretch as the chain wears.

parts.name: Flywheel rotor (magneto)
parts.description: A steel cup bolted to the crank taper with six permanent magnets on its inner rim. As it spins around the fixed stator coils it generates alternating current, and its mass smooths out the single cylinder's uneven power pulses. A raised bar on the outside triggers the pickup coil once per revolution.

specs.label: Output
specs.value: AC, roughly 12 V lighting, 100-250 V exciter

parts.name: Stator coils
parts.description: Six coils wound on a laminated iron core, bolted to the left crankcase cover so they never turn. Five feed the lighting and charging circuit. The darker exciter coil at the bottom has a denser winding of thinner wire, which gives the higher voltage the CDI unit needs to fire the plug.

specs.label: Exciter coil
specs.value: Fine wire, many turns, 100-250 V AC

parts.name: Pickup coil
parts.description: A small magnet wrapped in a coil of wire, mounted just outside the rotor. When the reluctor bar on the rotor sweeps past, it induces a short voltage pulse that tells the CDI unit exactly when to fire.

parts.name: CDI unit
parts.description: Capacitive discharge ignition. A capacitor inside charges from the exciter coil. When the pickup pulse arrives, a silicon controlled rectifier switches and dumps the stored charge into the ignition coil in one burst. The kill switch simply shorts the exciter feed to ground.

parts.name: Ignition coil
parts.description: A step-up transformer. A few hundred turns on the primary side, many thousands on the secondary. It multiplies the CDI pulse up to 200 times, to the 20,000 volts or more that the plug gap needs.

parts.name: Ignition wiring
parts.description: Red carries exciter coil voltage to the CDI, blue carries the pickup pulse, yellow runs from the CDI to the ignition coil, and the thick black high-tension lead feeds the plug cap. Watch them flash each time the plug fires.

parts.name: Starter driven gear and one-way clutch
parts.description: A roller-type one-way clutch. When the starter turns the 46-tooth outer race, six spring-loaded rollers wedge between it and the inner race on the crank and drive the engine. Once the engine fires and the inner race overtakes, the rollers drop back and the starter gear freewheels, so the motor is never over-spun.

parts.name: Starter reduction gear
parts.description: A double gear that multiplies starter motor torque. The 42-tooth gear is driven by the 10-tooth motor pinion and the 14-tooth gear drives the starter clutch. Overall the motor turns about 14 times for each crank revolution.

parts.name: Starter motor
parts.description: A 12 V brushed DC motor fed from the battery through the starter relay. It only turns while the button is held. The cutaway shows its armature spinning inside the case.

parts.name: Kickstarter lever and spindle
parts.description: Pushing the lever down turns the spindle. A helical spline on the spindle forces the 30-tooth kick gear to slide sideways into mesh before it starts to turn it, then a return spring brings everything back and the gear slides out of mesh again.

parts.name: Kick idle gear
parts.description: A 22-tooth gear that freewheels on the mainshaft and is locked by lugs to the back of the clutch basket. When the kick gear slides into it, the kick drives the clutch basket, the basket drives the primary gear, and the primary gear turns the crank. Because it bypasses the clutch plates, the engine can be kicked in any gear with the clutch pulled.

parts.name: Balancer shaft
parts.description: A single cylinder shakes because the piston stops and reverses twice per revolution. This shaft carries an offset weight and is geared to the crank at 1 : 1 but turning the opposite way, so its weight cancels much of the primary vibration.

parts.name: Clutch basket and primary driven gear
parts.description: The 67-tooth primary driven gear is riveted to the basket through rubber dampers. It is always driven by the 18-tooth gear on the crank but freewheels on the mainshaft, so on its own it passes no power to the gearbox. The friction plates ride in its slots.

parts.name: Clutch inner hub
parts.description: Splined to the gearbox mainshaft, so whatever turns the hub turns the gearbox input. Grooves on its outside drive the steel plates. Four posts take the bolts that hold the clutch springs.

parts.name: Friction plates (5)
parts.description: Aluminium plates faced with friction material, with tabs on the outside that slide in the basket slots. They always turn with the basket, so with the engine running they spin at engine speed divided by 3.72.

parts.name: Steel plates (4)
parts.description: Plain steel plates with teeth on the inside that slide on the inner hub grooves. They always turn with the hub and the mainshaft. Squeeze them against the friction plates and the two sets lock together; release the pressure and they slip freely.

parts.name: Pressure plate
parts.description: Clamps the plate stack against the hub. The four springs push it inwards. Pulling the lever pushes it outwards via the push rod, which unloads the stack and disconnects the engine from the gearbox.

parts.name: Clutch springs and bolts
parts.description: Four coil springs held by bolts screwed into the inner hub posts. Their preload is what makes the plates grip. Weak or sagged springs are the most common cause of clutch slip on a hard-worked commuter bike.

parts.name: Clutch push rod
parts.description: Runs through a hole bored down the centre of the mainshaft. The lifter arm on the left pushes one end and the other end lifts the pressure plate on the right.

parts.name: Clutch actuator arm and cable
parts.description: The clutch cable from the handlebar lever pulls this arm and rotates its spindle. A flat cut into the spindle bears on the end of the push rod and shoves it towards the clutch.

parts.name: Mainshaft with 1st gear
parts.description: The gearbox input shaft. The clutch hub is splined to its right-hand end, so it only turns when the clutch is engaged. Its 13-tooth first gear is machined as part of the shaft. The shaft is hollow for the clutch push rod.

parts.name: Countershaft (output shaft)
parts.description: The gearbox output shaft. The front sprocket sits on its left-hand end outside the crankcase, so it turns whenever the rear wheel turns. Its gears are either splined to it or freewheel on it.

parts.name: M2, mainshaft 2nd gear
parts.description: 17 teeth, splined to the mainshaft and held in place by a circlip. It always drives C2 on the countershaft. In 2nd gear the C4 slider locks C2 to the countershaft.

parts.name: M3, mainshaft 3rd gear (slider)
parts.description: 20 teeth, splined to the mainshaft so it can slide sideways while always turning with the shaft. Dog teeth on both faces lock it to M4 (4th gear) or M5 (5th gear). As a plain gear it drives C3 in 3rd.

parts.name: M4, mainshaft 4th gear
parts.description: 23 teeth, freewheeling on a bush on the mainshaft. It is always turned by C4. In 4th gear the M3 slider moves left, its dogs enter these windows, and M4 becomes locked to the mainshaft.

parts.name: M5, mainshaft 5th gear
parts.description: 25 teeth, freewheeling on the mainshaft and always turned by C5. In 5th gear the M3 slider moves right and locks it. This pair is an overdrive: the countershaft turns faster than the mainshaft.

parts.name: C1, countershaft 1st gear
parts.description: The biggest gear in the box, 36 teeth, freewheeling on the countershaft and always driven by the 13-tooth M1. In 1st gear the C5 slider moves right and its dogs lock C1 to the countershaft.

parts.name: C5, countershaft 5th gear (slider)
parts.description: 24 teeth, splined to the countershaft. It is the slider for 1st gear: its dogs face C1. As a plain gear it is driven by M5 when 5th is selected.

parts.name: C3, countershaft 3rd gear
parts.description: 29 teeth, freewheeling on the countershaft and always driven by M3. In 3rd gear the C4 slider moves right and locks it.

parts.name: C4, countershaft 4th gear (slider)
parts.description: 26 teeth, splined to the countershaft with dogs on both faces. Sliding left it locks C2 for 2nd gear, sliding right it locks C3 for 3rd. As a plain gear it is driven by M4 in 4th.

parts.name: C2, countershaft 2nd gear
parts.description: 32 teeth, freewheeling on the countershaft and always driven by M2. In 2nd gear the C4 slider moves left and locks it.

parts.name: Shift drum
parts.description: A drum with three channels cut around it. A pin on each shift fork rides in one channel, so as the drum turns the channels push the forks sideways. The channel shapes decide which dog clutch moves at each drum position and make sure each one returns to neutral before the next engages.

parts.name: Star cam and stopper arm
parts.description: The star plate on the end of the drum has a valley for every gear. A spring-loaded roller on the stopper arm drops into the valleys and holds the drum exactly in place. A roller cannot rest on a ridge, so the drum can never stop between gears. The one exception is the ridge between 1st and 2nd, which is ground flat so the roller can rest there: that flat is neutral, which is why it sits half a click between 1st and 2nd.

parts.name: Countershaft fork, 1st
parts.description: Sits in the groove of the C5 slider. Its channel moves it only once, to push C5 against C1 for 1st gear.

parts.name: Countershaft fork, 2nd/3rd
parts.description: Sits in the groove of the C4 slider. Its channel moves it left for 2nd gear and right for 3rd, returning through the middle in between.

parts.name: Mainshaft fork
parts.description: Sits in the groove of the M3 slider on the mainshaft. Its pin rides in the drum's right-hand channel and moves M3 left for 4th and right for 5th.

parts.name: Fork shafts
parts.description: Plain ground shafts fixed in the crankcase. The forks slide along them, steered only by their pins in the drum channels.

parts.name: Gearshift spindle, pedal and ratchet
parts.description: The gear pedal turns this spindle a few degrees. Its ratchet arm on the right catches a pin on the star plate and rotates the drum one step, then a centring spring returns the spindle and pedal for the next shift. The pedal always comes back to the same place, which is why this is called a return shift.

parts.name: Neutral switch
parts.description: A contact screwed into the crankcase opposite the end of the drum. In neutral a pin on the drum touches it and earths the green neutral lamp on the dashboard. The lamp here lights when the drum reaches neutral.

parts.name: Front sprocket
parts.description: 14 teeth, on the left end of the countershaft outside the crankcase. It drives the rear sprocket through a 428 chain. Changing it by one tooth changes overall gearing by about 7 percent.

specs.label: Chain
specs.value: 428 (12.7 mm pitch shown as 15.9 mm 520 equivalent)

parts.name: Drive chain
parts.description: Carries power from the front sprocket to the rear wheel. The top run is the tight side, pulled forward by the front sprocket. Only a short length is drawn here.
